text:
To: Programme Managers
From: Lucian Moreau, Quality Assurance
Subject: Supplier audit findings

The audit of our three principal component suppliers was completed last week. Two met every requirement; the third, Delvaux Metals, fell short in several respects. [1] In particular, its records of batch testing were incomplete, which makes it impossible to trace defective parts to their origin.

Delvaux has been given sixty days to submit a corrective action plan. [2] we receive no satisfactory response, orders will be transferred to an alternative supplier. In the meantime, programme managers should [3] incoming deliveries from Delvaux with particular care and report any anomaly at once. Please note that the audit report is confidential and must not be [4] outside the company.

choices: The deficiencies identified are serious enough to put at risk the certification on which our own products depend.
The deficiencies identified are minor enough to be remedied without any change to the supplier's own procedures.
The deficiencies identified were serious enough to have put at risk the certification held by the other two suppliers.
The strengths identified are significant enough to support the certification on which our own products depend.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'In particular', which narrows down a general statement of serious shortcomings; the first option gives that statement. The others minimize the problems, attribute the risk to other suppliers, or describe strengths.
'Should we receive no satisfactory response' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if we receive'; 'whereas', 'albeit' and 'insofar' cannot introduce this condition.
Managers should 'inspect' deliveries with care; 'inspire', 'insert' and 'insure' do not fit.
A confidential report must not be 'disclosed' (revealed) outside the company; 'disposed', 'displaced' and 'dispensed' do not fit.

text:
Lakeshore Conference Centre

Choosing a venue for a corporate event involves more than counting seats. At Lakeshore, we recognize that the success of a meeting depends on [1] details that delegates seldom notice but always feel: natural light, reliable connectivity, and rooms in which people can hear one another without effort.

[2] Our nine rooms, which accommodate between ten and four hundred guests, can be reconfigured overnight, and our in-house team handles every aspect of catering and equipment. [3] it is a board retreat or an international congress, a single coordinator will oversee your event from the first inquiry to the final invoice. Enquiries received [4] 15 May qualify for a ten percent reduction on autumn bookings.

questions.explanation: 'Subtle details' are small, delicate things that delegates seldom notice; the other adjectives do not match 'seldom notice but always feel'.

choices: Flexibility of this kind is easy to find in any venue, and it is one of the reasons clients leave us.
Flexibility of this kind is difficult to find in a single venue, and it is one of the reasons clients return to us.
Rigidity of this kind is difficult to find in a single venue, and it is one of the reasons clients return to us.
Flexibility of this kind is difficult to afford in a single venue, and it is one of the reasons clients complain.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes rooms that can be reconfigured overnight, which is flexibility; only the first option leads into it coherently. The others contradict the advertisement or describe rigidity.
'Whether it is a board retreat or an international congress' presents two alternatives; the others cannot present options.
'Enquiries received before 15 May' gives the deadline for the reduction; 'during' and 'within' do not fit a fixed date and 'until' would suggest continuing up to it.

text:
Dear Dr. Fontaine,

I am writing to confirm the arrangements for your forthcoming lecture at the Institute on 21 November. We should be [1] if you could arrive by 5 p.m., so that the technical team may test the equipment and brief you on the layout of the auditorium.

[2] The lecture is scheduled to begin at 6.30 p.m. and to last approximately fifty minutes, followed by questions from the audience. [3] your fee, we shall pay it by bank transfer within fourteen days of the event, together with any travel costs that you have [4].

Yours sincerely,
Renata Illes
Programme Coordinator

questions.explanation: 'We should be grateful if you could' is the polite formula; 'gracious' describes manner and 'graceful' describes movement.

choices: The audience is expected to exclude around two hundred students and members of the public, none of whom have read your latest book.
The audience is expected to include around two hundred students and members of the public, most of whom have read your latest book.
The audience was expected to include around two hundred students, most of whom would read your latest book.
The lecture is expected to include around two hundred students and members of the public, most of whom have read your latest book.
questions.explanation: The next sentence gives the timing of the lecture, so the previous one introduces the audience; only the first is coherent and well formed. The others contradict themselves, use mismatched tenses, or confuse lecture and audience.
'As for your fee' introduces a new topic, meaning regarding; 'as of' refers to a date and 'as if' compares.
Travel costs are 'incurred' when a person has to pay them; 'inferred' means deduced, 'induced' means caused, and 'injured' means harmed.
